headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because Airbyte can move business data broadly while next-ai-draw-io can browse, use MCP, and send content to third-party model APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can ingest and transform business data, and B can browse and use MCP, so a shared file or pasted artifact could carry instructions from A into B. The pair lacks documented isolation or provenance controls, but no direct shared channel is explicit, so this is an inferred medium-risk pathway rather than high.
conditions: IF A outputs text that B later opens as a prompt or instruction source
IF the operator bridges them through a shared file, clipboard, or MCP resource
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Disable MCP access in B for untrusted artifacts
Require a human review step before B reads A-generated text
Use a read-only export format from A
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to A outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: A handles business data and has broad network egress; B handles PDFs, text, images, and API keys, and can send content to multiple external model providers. If data from A is passed into B, B can exfiltrate it to third-party APIs by default, creating a sensitive-data leakage path with broad blast radius.
conditions: IF business data from A is opened or pasted into B
IF B is configured to use any external model provider listed in its API surfaces
mitigations: Do not route sensitive A data into B
Configure B to use a local-only model backend
Remove API keys from B before processing A data
Use a separate non-sensitive staging copy
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on B inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has broad network egress and API access, while B has broad network egress, browser use, MCP, and multiple external model backends. Their overlapping write-like influence is indirect rather than a shared filesystem write, but both can mutate external services or shared resources if pointed at the same targets, so conflict risk exists in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents are configured against the same external API, workspace, or MCP resource
IF concurrent runs are allowed without locking or coordination
mitigations: Assign separate credentials to A and B
Serialize writes to shared external resources
Disable concurrent runs on the same target
Use per-agent staging environments
requires-engineering: add resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce transformed business data, and B is designed for natural-language, AI-assisted visualization and can act on content through browsers and MCP. That makes it plausible for B to treat A's output as authoritative without verification, but the profiles do not show direct autonomous action-taking, so medium is the appropriate conservative choice.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated text or diagrams as source-of-truth
IF the operator does not insert a verification step between A and B
mitigations: Require manual validation of A outputs before B uses them
Mark A outputs as untrusted in B
Limit B to rendering only, not decision-making
Keep an audit trail of source artifacts
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: A touches business data, while B handles PDFs, text, images, diagrams, and explicitly requests API keys and environment variables, which can create retention and residency mismatches when the same data class flows through both. No specific jurisdictional mismatch is documented, so this is a medium compliance risk rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated or sensitive business data from A is processed by B
IF B's external model providers retain prompts or uploads longer than A's policy allows
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from B
Review provider retention settings before use
Rotate any API keys used by B
Document data-flow boundaries between A and B
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
